In [[geometry]], the '''trigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|75}}}}). It contains 20 [[triangle]]s, 30 [[square]]s and 12 [[pentagon]]s. It is also a [[Midsphere#Canonical polyhedron|canonical polyhedron]].

{{Johnson solid}}

It can be constructed as a [[rhombicosidodecahedron]] with three [[pentagonal cupola]]e rotated through 36 degrees. Related Johnson solids are:
* The [[gyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|72}}}}) where one cupola is rotated;
* The [[parabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|73}}}}) where two opposing cupolae are rotated;
* And the [[metabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|74}}}}) where two non-opposing cupolae are rotated.
